children: The search-side projection seam that the Content Graph is modeled as the dual of — both project content, one into an index, one into edges.

Indx Retriever Seam is the abstraction the Indx Engine exposes for search: a clean boundary where content is projected into a retrievable index rather than queried in place. Each surface that holds searchable text contributes through it, and the engine materializes a unified index behind it. It is the search half of Barkpark's "project, don't query live" philosophy — the seam Search swaps in via engine=indx without the caller noticing.

of this seam. Set them side by side:

| | Indx Retriever Seam | Content Graph | |---|---|---| | Projects content into | a search index | directed edges | | Per-surface callback | indexer contribution | Edge Extractor | | Async materializer | IndexerWorker | Edge Projector | | Materialized store | search index | Content Edges Table | | Read surface | Postgres Search | Graph Traversal / Graph View |
Reading the table top-to-bottom, every row of the search machinery has a graph twin. That symmetry isn't accidental — the graph was built by holding the retriever seam up as a mirror.

Treating both as projections means the same discipline applies: writes enqueue async work (Oban Workers), reads hit a clean materialized surface, and the request hot path stays cheap. The seam is the conceptual seed the whole Content Graph grew from.
